Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

MedXpertQA: Benchmarking Expert-Level Medical Reasoning and Understanding · documents: The v1 paper assesses leakage risk before and after rewriting with GPT-4o outputs, using perplexity and similarity to collected explanations measured by ROUGE-L and edit distance.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

MedXpertQA: Benchmarking Expert-Level Medical Reasoning and Understanding · documents: The v1 methods describe model rephrasing intended to preserve question information, removal of weak distractors and setting the final choice counts to ten for Text and five for MM, using GPT-4o-2024-11-20 and Claude-3.5-Sonnet-20241022.

candidate.normal18.medxpertqa.paper.model-augmentation.binding-correction-v2

  • Original author-stage note: Actual new author-only source-content proposal. Distinct source-verifier/adversarial exact-digest reviews and coordinator admission are pending. No replication, independently adjudicated rights, commercial supplier credit, or deep credit is implied.
  • The introduction refers to three proprietary augmentation models, whereas this methods stage explicitly names two.
  • Most MM questions already contain five choices, often dependent on images, and the methods say these choices cannot be expanded; the final choice count does not mean extra choices were generated for those questions.
  • The author does not invent a third model's identity or role, or treat rewriting as proof of unseen content.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

MedXpertQA: Benchmarking Expert-Level Medical Reasoning and Understanding · documents: The v1 paper describes filtering an initial 37,543-question medical exam/textbook bank using model votes, difficulty thresholds based on human-response Brier scores and prior expert difficulty ratings, and semantic-similarity filtering.

candidate.normal18.medxpertqa.paper.question-filtering

  • Original author-stage note: Actual new author-only source-content proposal. Distinct source-verifier/adversarial exact-digest reviews and coordinator admission are pending. No replication, independently adjudicated rights, commercial supplier credit, or deep credit is implied.
  • The paper reports that approximately 16.78% of questions lacked the needed human-response/difficulty annotations and did not undergo that filtering stage. This does not mean they skipped the separately described final physician review. Model voters are not human annotators; filtering does not demonstrate clinical reliability.
